source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Structure-Aware Numerical Reasoning in LLaMA 3.1 8B
source.authors: Rahul Chowdhury; Timothy A. Rupprecht; Sen-Hao Cao; Jia-Hao Liu; Octavia I. Camps; David Bau; Pu Zhao; Yan-Zhi Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests a related induction mechanism with probing and activation patching, but on latent numerical differences in LLaMA 3.1–8B rather than token-copying induction heads in small attention-only transformers.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no training-time or loss-curve results, no token-index in-context-learning measure, and no few-shot task-learning results. Its sequence-prediction MAE and R² describe task performance but do not by themselves measure the specified induction mechanism. The paper describes head-level patching setup, but reports no individual head identities or head-specific outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study does not test V1–V7. It studies a delta-retrieval mechanism in LLaMA 3.1–8B, which the authors call analogous to induction. The task was built so token-level induction-head copying cannot solve it. It names no heads, no previous-token head and no composition, and has no training dynamics or token-index ICL measure. The finding is a related but different construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim this is among the first studies to identify 'concept induction' in LLMs. They describe the mechanism as analogous to induction heads, operating at a structural rather than token level. They report no individual induction heads.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a designed numerical sequence task, linear probes, and activation/key patching on a pretrained LLaMA model; it does not reproduce the original small attention-only training setup or its training-time measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Patching effects are reported from layer 14 onward; key swaps at positions 25 and 27 shift confidence but do not reverse the ground-truth preference.

fits_no_version.finding: LLaMA 3.1–8B stores first differences locally, at position 27 from about layer 7. The final query causally retrieves that delta from layer 14 on, and the model adds it to the last number. Key swaps between positions 25 and 27 shift confidence but do not flip the prediction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large pretrained LLMs perform induction-like retrieval over latent, non-token structure (e.g. numerical first differences), not only token-level copying.

record.problems: The mechanistic tests use one model and a specially designed numerical task. Patching and token-importance analyses use 100 instances selected with zero MAE. Several outcomes are presented only in figures, and the paper reports no uncertainty estimates or individual head identities.
record.rows_left_out: The overall sequence-prediction MAE of 4.2748 and R² of 0.9958 are omitted because they measure task performance, not the induction mechanism or the claim’s in-context-learning measure. No individual attention-head patching results are reported.

untested.parts: Small attention-only transformers, previous-token head composition, and literal [A][B]…[A]→[B] token copying. The task was designed to exclude token copying.
No token-index in-context-learning loss measure and no head ablations on ICL.
No identified induction heads in LLaMA. One model only.
No variation of data or training.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 'supports' label is removed. The study's task was deliberately built so token-level induction heads cannot solve it, and no head-level or previous-token-composition evidence is reported. Patching and key-swap analyses use 100 zero-MAE instances, with figure-only results and no uncertainty. Head-level patching is described (Fig. 9), but only aggregated token-importance results appear.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test small attention-only transformers, composition with an earlier previous-token head, or literal [A][B] … [A] → [B] token copying. It tests an analogous mechanism over latent first differences in one LLaMA model.

rows.subject: LLaMA 3.1–8B
rows.size_stated: 8B; 32 layers and 32 attention heads per layer
rows.operation_detail: Fit linear regressors to decode the first difference from the 27th token position across layers.

conditions.value: across layers; text says decodability starts after layer 7 and remains relatively stable across the first 16 layers
4,500 training samples and 500 held-out test samples

rows.value: figure only; text says MAE drops sharply after layer 7 and R² stabilizes above 0.8
rows.note: Shows that the difference is linearly decodable at the specified location; probing alone does not establish functional induction or copying.
rows.check: Probes decodability of a latent first difference in an 8B model, not induction heads or token copying. Baseline is missing: the text compares against shuffled-label control probes and a cross-position control.

rows.subject: LLaMA 3.1–8B
rows.size_stated: 8B; 32 layers and 32 attention heads per layer
rows.operation_detail: Use activations at the 57th token position to decode the first difference associated with the 27th position.
rows.value: figure only; text says R² is negative and MAE is high, with no meaningful linear relationship
rows.check: Cross-position control probe for the latent-difference construct. It does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: LLaMA 3.1–8B
rows.size_stated: 8B; 32 layers and 32 attention heads per layer
rows.operation_detail: Fit linear regressors to decode the final number from the 57th token position across layers.

conditions.value: across layers; text says decodability declines after layer 8
4,500 training samples and 500 held-out test samples

rows.value: figure only; text says the number is linearly decodable, with MAE increasing and R² decreasing after layer 8
rows.note: Probes a numerical component used in the paper’s proposed arithmetic composition; this is representational evidence, not a direct test of induction.
rows.check: Probes final-number decodability. This is an arithmetic component, not induction. Shuffled-label control baseline not recorded.

rows.subject: LLaMA 3.1–8B
rows.size_stated: 8B; 32 layers and 32 attention heads per layer
rows.operation_detail: Use activations at the 27th token position to decode the final number at the 57th position.
rows.value: figure only; text says performance is consistently poor
rows.check: Cross-position control for final-number decoding. It does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: LLaMA 3.1–8B
rows.size_stated: 8B; 32 layers and 32 attention heads per layer
rows.operation_detail: Patch clean-run hidden states at token positions and the final token's query into a flat, all-100 corrupt sequence; compare probability of the counterfactual next number with the unpatched corrupt run.

conditions.value: repeating first-difference sequence versus flat sequence of 100s
effect at token 27 begins from layer 14 onward; query patch begins one layer above the hidden-state patch

rows.measure: Difference in probability assigned to counterfactual label 100 + Δ*
rows.value: figure only; text reports a significant increase at token 27 from layer 14 onward
rows.note: Authors interpret this as causal retrieval of the locally stored first difference by the final query.
rows.check: Retrieval of a latent delta at position 27, from layer 14 on. This is analogous to induction over latent structure, not the V1 token-level head circuit in small attention-only models. No heads or previous-token composition are identified.

rows.subject: LLaMA 3.1–8B
rows.size_stated: 8B; 32 layers and 32 attention heads per layer
rows.operation_detail: Combine causal effects of patched attention-head outputs with value-weighted attention to rank token positions by importance.
rows.note: The text identifies position 27 as the difference to be added, position 33 as the onset of the repeating pattern, and the other listed positions as relevant to alignment or extrapolation. No individual attention-head results are stated.
rows.check: Token importance positions aggregated over heads. No head identities. Bears on the latent-delta mechanism only.

rows.subject: LLaMA 3.1–8B
rows.size_stated: 8B; 32 layers and 32 attention heads per layer
rows.operation_detail: Swap keys at positions 27 and 25 from layer l onward while preserving their value vectors.

conditions.value: swap K27 and K25; preserve V27 and V25

rows.measure: Change in probability of the counterfactual label relative to the corrupt run
rows.value: figure only; text reports a significant increase, but the counterfactual probability does not overtake the ground-truth probability
rows.note: The intervention shifts confidence toward the alternative difference but does not make it the more probable prediction.
rows.check: Key-swap probes positional versus delta cues in the latent mechanism. It does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: LLaMA 3.1–8B
rows.size_stated: 8B; 32 layers and 32 attention heads per layer
rows.operation_detail: Swap keys at positions 27 and 25 from layer l onward while preserving their value vectors.

conditions.value: swap K27 and K25; preserve V27 and V25

rows.measure: Change in probability of the ground-truth label relative to the corrupt run and absolute post-intervention probability
rows.value: figure only; text reports a drop in ground-truth confidence, but its post-intervention probability remains above the counterfactual probability
rows.note: The authors say key-based positional cues influence retrieval but do not override the original delta-based composition.
rows.check: Key-swap effect on ground-truth confidence. It does not bear on any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LLaMA 3.1–8B on the paper’s repeated-first-difference numerical sequence task
reader_labels.reason: Patching identifies a causal effect at the position storing the needed difference, and the token-importance and key-swap results are consistent with structural delta retrieval and composition (R5–R8).
